Answer: C
Reason: Figure 2 demonstrates a visible visceral pleural line in the right hemithorax with an absence of lung markings peripherally and increased radiolucency, which are classic radiographic signs of a pneumothorax. This finding explains the sudden onset of pain and clinical worsening, distinguishing it from pneumonia or ARDS which would present with opacities rather than hyperlucency.
